title: VPC stateful upgrade orchestration notes
body:
Context and intent:

This note collects a proposal and operational runbook fragments for performing safe upgrades of stateful components in private (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped) deployments. Focus is on CI/CD mechanics (Helm + ArgoCD), artifact provenance (image signing / attestation), Terraform module patterns for upgrading platform infra, and practical rollback/rollback-safety for stateful workloads and DB migrations.

Why different from stateless upgrades?
- StatefulSets and DBs have ordering, data-migration, and availability constraints.
- Private deploy constraints: restricted egress, registry mirroring, stricter signing/attestation, longer change windows.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Customer clusters may be air-gapped or VPC-restricted; primary artifact distribution paths are private registries or signed bundles transported via approved channels.
- KMS/HSM-backed signing for images or SBOMs is mandatory for enterprise customers.
- ArgoCD is the GitOps engine in most installs; we own Helm charts and umbrella charts.
- Terraform manages infra (VPCs, registries, KMS integration, operator CRs).
- SRE/Customer runbook will require clear escalation steps and a rollback anchor in Git.

High-level pipeline (recommended pattern) – canonical flow:
1) Dev/PR: chart changes, values files, or Terraform module bump in a feature branch.
2) CI (cloud-based or CI runner inside customer network): lint charts, unit-test k8s manifests (kubeval), run terraform fmt/validate.
3) Build image(s) if change includes server binary: build in ephemeral runner, run unit/integration tests, create SBOM.
4) Sign artifact(s): cosign sign --key kms://projects/.. (or use offline cosign key in airgapped flow). Generate attestation and record digest.
5) Push to mirror/private registry OR export signed OCI tarball for airgap transfer.
6) Publish Git tag / update release manifest in infra repo with image digest(s) and SBOM links.
7) ArgoCD picks up the manifest (or manual promotion controls the Git commit that ArgoCD tracks).
8) Progressive rollout executes with preflight hooks, smoke checks, and canary gates.

Airgap specifics (two common models):
- Mirror model: CI pushes to customer-private registry over a secured pipeline (bastion). Requires registry credentials vaulted in CI.
- Bundle export model: CI emits signed OCI tarball + attestations + SBOM. Ops transfers bundle to customer via S3/airgap appliance and loads into registry (registry-side attestation verify).

Image signing + attestation recommendations:
- Use cosign for image signatures; store private keys in KMS when possible. For air-gapped installs, provide an offline signing key signer tool with strict access logs.
- Verify signatures in ArgoCD by enabling image policy webhook that rejects unsigned or mismatched digests.
- Record SBOMs and attestations as part of the release commit (link in values.yaml or a release manifest file).

Terraform module upgrade pattern (notes / example snippet):
- Modules should expose: image_digest, chart_version, values_override_map, registry_mirroring_config.
- Do NOT directly mutate in-cluster state from Terraform; prefer to update GitOps manifests which ArgoCD will apply. Terraform should manage platform infra and Git repository resources.

Example module usage pattern (pseudo HCL included for clarity):
terraform {
  required_providers {
    null = { source = "hashicorp/null" }
  }
}
module "redwood_app_release" {
  source = "git::ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//argocd-app"
  app_name = "redwood-core"
  target_repo = "gitops/customer-cluster/apps"
  chart_version = "1.12.0"
  image_digest = "sha256:abcd1234..."
  values_overrides = {
    replicaCount = 3
    imagePullPolicy = "IfNotPresent"
  }
}

Notes: Terraform modifies the GitOps repo (via a controlled ci user) to update the ArgoCD tracked commit. ArgoCD performs the actual cluster mutation. This provides an auditable commit history and a safe rollback anchor (revert the commit).

Helm / ArgoCD rollout strategy for stateful components:
- Use a combination of Helm hooks, ArgoCD rollouts (or K8s Canary via Flagger), and built-in pre/post hooks.
- Preferred for complex stateful upgrades: serialized partitioned rolling update with single-pod-at-a-time and explicit preStop hooks to flush connections.
- Example Helm values to control upgrade behavior:
  updateStrategy: "OnDelete"
  partitionedRollout: true
  rolloutBatchSize: 1
  preUpgradeHookJob: true

- PodDisruptionBudgets should be conservative during upgrade windows to avoid accidental eviction cascades.
- For databases: prefer in-place, phased migrations using a migration controller CR or migration Job with a leader election/lock.

DB migration orchestration patterns (recommendation):
- Zero-downtime migrations: prefer backward-compatible changes (add columns, create new tables) and follow with a secondary step that migrates reads to new schema.
- Two-step upgrade: deploy code that can work with old and new schema, run migration job, then flip traffic.
- Migration runbook fragment:
  1) Run schema-change job with dry-run -> capture duration and lock time.
  2) Run migration in blue-green batch on replica(s) where possible.
  3) Verify replica sync and replay lag metrics.
  4) Promote primary after sanity checks.

Health checks, smoke tests and automated gating:
- Preflight (blocking): chart lint, kubeval, terraform validate, unit tests, signature verification.
- Pre-deploy smoke: deploy to ephemeral namespace or canary namespace and run smoke tests (health endpoints, small synthetic queries).
- Post-deploy checks (gating metrics):
  - 5xx rate for service <= baseline + threshold
  - p99 latency within 1.5x baseline
  - error budget consumption delta small
  - DB replication lag below X ms
- Gating implementation: integrate Argo Rollouts or external canary orchestration that consults Prometheus or Datadog metrics and automatically promotes or rolls back.

Rollback mechanics and fast exit points:
- Keep a clear git commit anchor for the last-known-good manifest. Rollback = revert git commit (Terraform revert if used to mutate Git). ArgoCD will sync back.
- For DB-affecting releases: plan compensating migration or pre-migration snapshot; if rollback is required after destructive migration, require a manual restoration runbook (this must be tolerated as a last resort).
- Ensure existence of image retention policy for last known good images in the private registry.

Operational runbook (short actionable checklist for a typical upgrade window):
- Pre-window (24–72h): schedule window, announce to customer SREs, snapshot current manifests, tag last-known-good in Git.
- Pre-flight (1–2h): run smoke on canary namespace, validate cosign signatures, run terraform plan for infra delta.
- Deploy canary (10–30m): apply 1 instance of updated stateful component to canary namespace or node pool. Run full integration smoke tests.
- Slow progressive rollout (1–4h): apply partitioned upgrade batches; after each batch run post-checks and metric gating.
- DB migration step (if present): run migration job during low-traffic sub-window; monitor replication lag and throttling.
- Rollback criteria: any gate failed OR critical 5xx spike OR p50/p99 regression beyond threshold. Execute revert commit and track rollback progress.
- Post-window: run extended monitoring for 24–72h, collect artifacts (logs, traces), and open postmortem ticket for any incidents.

Runbook commands and quick references (examples):
- Verify image signature (local / airgap verifier):
  cosign verify --key k8s://namespaces/security/secrets/cosign-key myregistry.example.com/redwood/core@sha256:abcd1234

- Push signed bundle (mirror flow):
  skopeo copy --dest-creds $REG_USER:$REG_PASS oci-archive:bundle.tar oci://my-private-registry/repository

- Revert to a previous GitOps commit with terraform-managed repo (example):
  # fetch and checkout commit
  git clone git@github.com:customer/gitops.git
  cd gitops
  git checkout <last-known-good-sha>
  git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/auto-promote-for-argocd

Open questions / risks / decisions to make:
- Migration safety: do we require built-in DB backups/snapshots before every migration? (operational overhead vs recovery speed).
- Airgap signing model: enterprise customers want KMS-only keys; how to support both offline and KMS-backed signing in the same pipeline?
- Terraform -> GitOps authority model: do we allow Terraform to write directly to app repos, or must every change be code-reviewed with an approval gate?
- Rollout automation vs manual approvals: what percentage of customers want fully automated canaries vs manual promotion?

Next steps / action items:
- Prototype: build a small CI job that produces a signed OCI bundle + attestations and a small ArgoCD app that verifies the attestation prior to sync. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2024-11-29.
- Add a terraform module example in infra repo that demonstrates writing to a GitOps repo instead of mutating cluster resources. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 2024-12-06.
- Draft a short customer-facing runbook (1 pager) for upgrade windows showing checklist and rollback steps. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2024-12-04.

Notes and references:
- See PD-5412 (Jira) for customer request re: offline signing and airgap delivery.
- Reference repo: github.com/redwood-inference/argocd-gatekeeper (internal POC).
- Slack thread: #private-deploys -> thread ts 1723452345 for earlier discussion on migration locks.

Appendix: quick example Helm hook for serialized preStop flush (values snippet):
hooks:
  preStop:
    exec: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "/usr/local/bin/flush-connections.sh --timeout 30s"]

(End of draft)
